title: Emit a durable SUBMISSION event naming the submitting agent
description: Promoted from IDEA-0027 via PROMO-0013, on evidence from EXP-0008 and EXP-0009. MAP has no durable record of who submitted a task for review. db/claims.py submit_task() delegates to release_task(), which emits no event and sets claimed_by = NULL in the same UPDATE, so the authoring identity is destroyed and never recorded by the only sanctioned submit path. Measured: 50 approved tasks have no SUBMISSION event, and 36 of 69 approvals since 2026-07-15 (52%) lack one, so the rate is worsening rather than decaying from legacy. Worse than absent, the record actively misattributes: TASK-236's durable log still credits claude-lab-gome for work claude-lab-zaro submitted twice on 2026-07-23. This blocks INS-0039/IDEA-0026 (parked), which cannot re-key the no-self-review guards onto authorship that is not recorded. EXP-0009 proved the fix on a scratch DB: status UPDATE and commit, THEN append a canonical SUBMISSION event; return contract unchanged, exactly one event per submit, no duplicate when the guarded UPDATE matches no row. SEQUENCING: db/claims.py is a contended output path of TASK-268 and TASK-273; this task depends on both and must not start until they release. SCOPE LIMITS: does not change any review guard, does not backfill the 50 historical tasks, does not alter tasks.owner semantics.
acceptance_criteria: submit_task() through db/claims.py emits exactly one canonical SUBMISSION event naming the submitting agent as actor, with the task_id and a trace_id; the existing bool return contract and the resulting task row (SUBMITTED, claimed_by NULL) are unchanged.

The event is appended AFTER the status commit, so a crash loses the authorship record rather than recording a submission that never happened; a repeat submit whose guarded UPDATE matches no row emits no event.

Absence of a SUBMISSION event is documented as UNKNOWN AUTHOR, never as evidence that no self-review occurred; this is stated in the delivery note so any future guard consuming the event cannot infer innocence from absence.

Isolated tests in MAP_System/tests/test_submission_event.py cover: event emitted with correct actor, no duplicate on repeat submit, row state unchanged, and absence-means-unknown documented behaviour; registered in run_tests.sh and green.

validate_events.py --fail-on-new reports no NEW warnings from the added emission (the canonical type SUBMISSION is used, not TASK_SUBMITTED, which already trips the validator at events.jsonl line 2145).

Evidence recorded via the TASK-219 delivery-note template, citing EXP-0008 for the gap and EXP-0009 for the proven mechanism; reviewed by an independent reviewer who is neither the author nor claude-lab-bima.
